A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HeteroSpec, with matching core methods, models and benchmarks. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support a reliable comparison despite substantial expansion and reformatting.

before.justification: Sections 3 and 5 report original draft-acceptance profiling, benchmark comparisons, component ablations and hyperparameter experiments, including Figure 1 and Tables 1-3.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark experiments and adds entropy validation, stratification sensitivity, overhead profiling, hardware comparisons and temperature experiments in Appendices A.1-A.7.

M1.justification: The entropy metric, three-layer CART partitioning, adaptive drafting, pruning and graph caching remain. However, Equation (2) changes the stated weighting of the tree-splitting loss, revising the reported bin-learning objective. The PDFs do not establish whether its implementation changed. Dynamic Graph Optimization is renamed Dynamic Computational Adaptation without a demonstrated procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use MT-bench, HumanEval, GSM8K, Alpaca and CNN/Daily Mail, with the same task coverage. ShareGPT calibration and the mathematics-trained draft model are retained. New analyses reuse this coverage; hardware, temperature and tree-depth variations concern experimental settings.

E2.justification: EAGLE-3 remains the evaluated external speculative-decoding comparator, with autoregressive decoding providing the speedup reference. The added hardware and temperature comparisons retain this comparator set. Neural-network alternatives to CART are discussed but not experimentally compared.

E3.justification: Main experiments change from A800 80G to H20-3e 141G GPUs. Appendix A.6 retains A800 evaluation and adds L40 evaluation, while A.7 adds temperature=1 to the existing temperature=0 setting. New protocols measure three-layer versus four-to-six-layer partition overlap using Jaccard similarity and profile runtime components and memory.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations and alpha sweep, v2 adds broader heterogeneity profiling, direct entropy-metric validation, tree-depth sensitivity and explicit overhead analysis (Figures 3-4 and Tables 4-5). Hardware and temperature robustness are also examined. The serving discussion remains prospective rather than becoming a batching experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V2 adds point estimates and descriptive distributions without introducing statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive diagnostic, profiling, hardware and temperature results. Section 5's average speedup changes from 4.26× to 4.24× and acceptance length from 6.55 to 6.62 under different main hardware settings. Matched A800 results also change: Vicuna-13B on HumanEval goes from 5.24× and 8.68 accepted tokens in v1 Table 1 to 5.41× and 9.04 in v2 Table 6.

T1.justification: Equation (2) changes each partition's squared-residual multiplier from 1/|Dj| to |Dj|/|D|, producing a mathematically non-equivalent split objective. The entropy definition otherwise remains equivalent. The standard Jaccard formula and qualitative CART rationale do not introduce a new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: V1 reports 4.26× acceleration relative to autoregressive decoding and separately claims superiority to EAGLE-3. V2's abstract instead attributes 4.24× speedup to comparison with state-of-the-art methods such as EAGLE-3, although Section 5 and Table 1 still use autoregressive decoding as the reference. This materially strengthens the headline performance claim without corresponding support.

C2.justification: Appendices A.2-A.4 add substantive interpretations linking stable low-entropy behavior to CART's suitability and partition overlap to intrinsic complexity boundaries. A.6-A.7 discuss hardware portability and stochastic-decoding behavior. The existing EAGLE-only generalizability limitation and future serving integration are retained and relocated.

D1.justification: V2 documents additional H20-3e and L40 hardware configurations and specifies that profiling times accumulate across dataset cases while memory denotes average runtime usage. These are useful technical disclosures, but detailed training configurations and code/data access information are not substantially expanded.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to stronger draft models, dynamic draft structures and serving systems remain the same. Bibliographic formatting changes and relocation of the serving discussion do not introduce new research relationships.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, preliminaries and method descriptions undergo extensive rewriting, with renamed modules and revised explanatory organization. Section 5.4 moves to Appendix A.8; the former appendix limitations paragraph becomes main-text Section 8, while future work moves to A.9.

P2.justification: The paper changes from single-column to two-column layout, revises annotations and captions in Figures 1-2, and adds multi-panel Figures 3-4. New sensitivity, profiling, hardware and temperature tables substantially expand the visual presentation, with A800 results appearing in Appendix Table 6.

improvement.justification: The added entropy validation, tree-depth sensitivity analysis and measured runtime/memory overhead address evidential gaps in v1's design and efficiency arguments, strengthening the empirical basis. The net improvement is limited by v2's misleading abstract attribution of 4.24× acceleration to EAGLE-3 rather than autoregressive decoding, and by its unexplained revision of the split-loss formula.
